children: Google is planning its largest-ever investment in Europe, committing at least €13B to expand its artificial intelligence infrastructure in Finland.

The investments over the next two years will include the construction of at least three new data centers as well as an expansion of Google’s existing facility in Hamina. new data centers will be built in Kajaani, Muhos and Vaala in northern part of the country.
The company is leveraging Finland’s cold climate and access to carbon-free electricity to support the expansion.

The project is expected to support more than 37,000 jobs across Finland during the construction phase and around 7,000 jobs once the facilities are operational, including employment among suppliers and local service providers.
“Google is proud to deepen our roots in Finland with the company’s largest single investment in Europe,” chief investment officer Ruth Porat said in a statement.

The investment is part of Alphabet’s broader push to expand its AI computing capacity. The company raised its 2026 capital spending forecast to as much as $205 billion in July, as it ramps up investment in infrastructure to keep pace with rivals in the race to lead the AI market.
The firm is also expanding the energy infrastructure supporting the projects, including a new wind-power agreement and a 94-megawatt battery storage system at its Kajaani site.

Utility Fortum Oyj has separately signed a 22-year power-purchase agreement with Google tied to the lifetime extension of the Loviisa nuclear power plant. The agreement, covering the period from 2030 through 2049, will account for 50% of the two-reactor plant’s capacity, Fortum said.

title: Google plans record €13B AI investment in Finland
